Series::exponential_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::exponential_() const
Series& Series::exponential_(double lambda) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with an independent nonnegative sample from an exponential distribution, whose density is lambda * exp(-lambda * x) for x >= 0. The no-argument form uses lambda = 1.

The exponential distribution models the waiting time until the next event when events arrive at a constant average rate. Internally each sample is drawn by the inverse-CDF method — x = -ln(U) / lambda for a uniform U in (0, 1] — so an exponential_ fill is a transformed uniform_ fill.

Like the other in-place samplers, the receiver supplies the shape, dtype, platform, and storage; its current values are discarded.

lambda is a rate, not a scale¶

lambda is the rate (events per unit time). The mean and the standard deviation are both 1 / lambda. Doubling lambda halves the typical waiting time. If you have a desired mean mu, pass lambda = 1 / mu.

Reproducibility¶

Deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling to fix the values; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each call advances a stream counter.

Parameters¶

lambda (double, default 1): the rate. Must be finite and > 0.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the samples. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity — every alias sees the values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is not floating-point (complex is not accepted, unlike normal_ / uniform_)

  • if lambda is non-finite or <= 0

Gradient¶

Not differentiable — a random overwrite carries no derivative through the replaced values or lambda.

Examples¶

Example 1. Default rate 1. Every sample is nonnegative. Seeded, so the values are fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({5}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.exponential_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.1699, 2.1792, 1.3738, 1.5186, 0.6553]

The distribution is right-skewed: most samples are small, with an occasional large one.

Example 2. lambda is a rate — over a large sample the mean and standard deviation are both close to 1 / lambda.

pluss::rng_seed(11);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.exponential_(4.0);
auto v = x.to_vec<double>();
double lo = 1e300, sum = 0;
for (double e : v) { lo = std::min(lo, e); sum += e; }
double mean = sum / v.size(), ss = 0;
for (double e : v) ss += (e - mean) * (e - mean);
std::cout << "min=" << lo << "  mean~" << mean
          << "  stddev~" << std::sqrt(ss / v.size()) << "\n";

Output¶

min=2.02657e-06  mean~0.249726  stddev~0.248912

1 / 4 = 0.25 for both moments. The smallest sample is a hair above zero; the support has no upper bound.

Example 3. lambda <= 0, a non-finite lambda, and a complex receiver are all rejected.

try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.exponential_(0.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.exponential_(-2.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto c = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Complex64);
  c.exponential_(1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

exponential_: expected a finite lambda > 0
exponential_: expected a finite lambda > 0
exponential_: receiver must have a floating-point dtype

Example 4. Reproducible under a fixed seed.

pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.exponential_(2.0);
pluss::rng_seed(5);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); b.exponential_(2.0);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "a == b: " << a.equal(b) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b: true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Pass a rate, not a mean. For mean mu, use lambda = 1 / mu.

  • lambda = 0 and negative rates are rejected.

  • Complex receivers are rejected (a difference from normal_ / uniform_); the dtype must be a real float.

  • Samples are nonnegative but have no upper bound — a fixed-size histogram or clamp may be needed downstream.

  • Reproducible only after pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream.

  • The trailing underscore marks the in-place mutation, not a distribution variant.

  • Not differentiable.

Summary¶

exponential_(lambda = 1) fills the receiver in place with exponential waiting-time samples:

  • density lambda * exp(-lambda*x) for x >= 0; lambda is a rate, mean = stddev = 1 / lambda

  • built by inverse-CDF from a uniform draw

  • real floating dtype only (no complex); not differentiable

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • Series::uniform_: the underlying uniform fill that exponential_ transforms.

  • Series::geometric_: the discrete analogue — a count of trials until the first success.

  • Series::log_normal_: another positive, right-skewed continuous fill.

  • pluss::series::poisson: counts of events in a fixed interval, the companion of exponential inter-arrival times.
